title: Does the hub PC itself have to pair or log in?
context: Decision 47 B made every device pair with a passkey and use Windows Hello or Face ID for big changes. Its first rollout locked Matt out of his own PC. Matt's call: his main PC is password-protected and at his house, he operates from it, and it shouldn't need a login. A local Claude Code session could reach the repo and the hub anyway, so guarding against local agents isn't worth the friction. Matt's refinements: nobody outside his computer may be able to spoof being the PC (the source is public); Face ID on the phone and a Windows passkey on the PC are fine for big changes; only the initial login must go. Amends decision 47: pairing and Face ID stay for remote devices (the phone over Tailscale). The PC's own browser is trusted. An off switch (a guard-off file in the hub folder, or CRUX_HUB_GUARD=off) turns the whole guard off.

options.name: The PC is trusted; only remote devices pair
options.summary: Requests that really come from the PC itself (loopback, not through Tailscale, never decided by a header the client sets) need no login, pairing or code. Big changes on the PC still ask for Windows Hello: the PC registers its passkey from the page on first use, with no code, and if Hello isn't available the change goes through with a push, so nothing can lock Matt out. The phone pairs once and uses Face ID for big changes. Off switch in the hub folder.
pros: No login on the machine Matt works from
The phone, which leaves the house, stays protected
cons: A local script can act as Matt again, as before decision 47; Matt accepts that

options.name: Keep decision 47 as built
options.summary: Every device pairs, the PC included.
cons: Locked Matt out on rollout; friction on his main machine

reason: Matt: "My main PC is where I operate from, I shouldn't have to log in from here." and "There needs to be some reasonableness to device security, since my PC is password protected and at my house."

settles.value: the machine the tool runs on is trusted (no login, no pairing); remote devices pair once with a passkey and use it for big changes; a file in the tool folder turns the guard off
